definitions.explanation: A period of silence observed to honor the dead or show respect, typically with eyes closed and head bowed. Common at memorial ceremonies and commemorative events.

examples.japanese: {黙祷|もくとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捧|ささ}げる→捧げる：02055_sasageru⟧。
examples.english: Offer a moment of silent prayer.

examples.japanese: ⟦{犠牲者|ぎせいしゃ}→犠牲者：18769_giseisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{一分間|いっぷんかん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{黙祷|もくとう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{行|おこな}われた→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: A one-minute moment of silence was held for the victims.

examples.japanese: ⟦{式典|しきてん}→式典：09526_shikiten⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{全員|ぜんいん}→全員：03310_zenin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{黙祷|もくとう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{始|はじ}まり→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧、⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{亡|な}くなった→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧⟦{方々|かたがた}→方々：02778_katagata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{偲|しの}んだ→偲ぶ：30130_shinobu⟧。
examples.english: The ceremony began with a moment of silence by all attendees, quietly remembering those who had passed away.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {黙|もく} (silence) and {祷|とう} (prayer). Used as both a noun and a suru verb ({黙祷|もくとう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧). At Japanese memorial services, the emcee typically announces {黙祷|もくとう} to signal the start and {黙祷|もくとう}やめ or お⟦{直|なお}り→直る：00735_naoru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧ to signal the end.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黙祷|もくとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捧|ささ}げる→捧げる：02055_sasageru⟧ (to offer a moment of silence)
- {黙祷|もくとう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to observe a moment of silence)
- {一分間|いっぷんかん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{黙祷|もくとう} (a one-minute moment of silence)
- {黙祷|もくとう}！ (Silence! — announcement at ceremonies)
